Authority Control — Finding the Registries That Actually Govern Your Document

Authority control means identifying your object in the shared registries that scholarship uses to disambiguate books, manuscripts, people, and places. The specific registries differ by tradition, and choosing the wrong one is a methodological error, not a harmless one.

Start with the general-purpose layer, which applies to almost everything:

  • VIAF (viaf.org) — international authority file for names (authors, scribes, printers, recipients). Aggregates national library authorities.
  • Wikidata (wikidata.org) — structured identifiers for persons, works, places, and institutions. Use the Q number.
  • Library of Congress authorities (id.loc.gov) — LCCN and name/title authorities; strong for printed material and American imprints.
  • GeoNames / GeoNames-style place registries — for the <origPlace> and <settlement> values in your header.

Then the tradition-specific layer. Here is where your three documents diverge:

Project Registries and identifier forms that apply
Jay
Dickinson manuscript		 Emily Dickinson Archive (edickinson.org) — the primary image and transcription registry; CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, with permission-free use for coursework.
Houghton Library call numbers, in the MS Am 1118.x series: MS Am 1118.3 = poems (fascicles + loose sheets); MS Am 1118.2 = Holland letters; MS Am 1118.4 = letters to various correspondents. Item form: MS Am 1118.3 [338].
Amherst College uses an AC accession scheme (e.g. AC 88-12).
Person authority: VIAF 31995584; Wikidata Q4441; LCCN n79054166.
Note: identifiers attach to the person, not to individual manuscripts. There is no item-level VIAF record for a single Dickinson poem.
Olyvia
French decree		 Archives nationales cotes (shelfmarks), cited by series letter and article number.
Gallica / BnF ARK identifiers — the form ark:/12148/<identifier>. An ARK is a persistent identifier: it names the object, not its current URL, so it survives the site being reorganised.
CALAMES for finding aids; FranceArchives as the cross-institutional portal.
Watch the genre vocabulary: édit, ordonnance, arrêt du Conseil, lettre patente, and déclaration are different instruments with different issuing authorities. Naming yours correctly is the authority work.
Andromeda
Peace and Friendship treaty		 Nova Scotia Archives reference numbers, cited as RG 1 volume 430 number 2, or O/S number 511 for oversize items. Search the Mi'kmaq Holdings Resource Guide.
Library and Archives Canada — Treaties, Surrenders and Agreements database. Search tip: the database requires historical spellings — try "Micmac" as well as "Mi'kmaq".
National Archives (UK), Colonial Office papers CO 217 — many surviving copies are here rather than in Canada.
ATRIS (Aboriginal and Treaty Rights Information System) for the modern rights context.
Note: Trismegistos, Pinakes, and Diktyon are Greek literary registries. They do not describe this document, and citing them would be an error.

The rule that makes this gradeable: name the registries that apply, record identifiers in the exact syntax you found them, and state why each registry governs your document. If you check a standard registry and find no record for your object, that is a legitimate and creditable finding — provided you show the search you made. A verified absence beats a padded citation list.
